R is a GIS ... or at least it can be! In this video lesson, which is a lecture rather than a code-along video, I cover:

* What a GIS is
* Coordinate Reference Systems (CRSs) ... this is super important
* Types of shapefiles -- points, lines, and polygons
* What a raster file is
* Core GIS concepts such as spatial grain and spatial extent (we will explore these concepts in depth in the future!)

:::{style="padding-top: 2em;"}

{{< video https://www.youtube.com/embed/NKvQxiwRBds?si=iyiAjEsqPj8Lav1I >}}

:::

## Take-home points

* A **geographic information system** (GIS) is a system for storing, managing, analyzing, and visualizing spatial data. R can serve as a GIS.
* A **coordinate reference system** (CRS) is the reference system that allows us to define the location of a geometry on the surface of the Earth. A pair of coordinates has no location without one.
* **Shapefiles** represent discrete features as points, lines, or polygons.
* A **raster** represents a region as a continuous grid of equally sized cells, where each cell stores a value.
* The **spatial extent** of a dataset is the area that the data cover, and the **spatial grain** is the finest spatial resolution of the data.

## Exercises

::: now_you
{{< fa user-circle size=2x >}} [Test your knowledge!]{style="font-size: 1.25em; padding-left: 0.5em;"}

After watching the lecture, use the questions below to evaluate your understanding. If an answer surprises you, please watch the relevant section of the video again!

1. True or false: A pair of coordinates defines a location on the surface of the Earth, with or without a coordinate reference system.

   `r torf(FALSE)`

2. A set of bird sampling locations is best represented by which type of shapefile?

   `r longmcq(c("Lines", answer = "Points", "Polygons", "A raster"))`

3. Elevation varies continuously across a landscape, and every location has a value. Which data model best represents it?

   `r longmcq(c("Points", "Lines", "Polygons", answer = "A raster"))`

4. A land cover dataset covers the conterminous United States with cells that are 30 meters on each side. Which term describes the area that the dataset covers?

   `r longmcq(c("The spatial grain", answer = "The spatial extent", "The coordinate reference system", "The geometry"))`
:::
